concept.name: Saga & Compensation Patterns
concept.tagline: Coordinate long-lived business transactions with compensating actions instead of distributed two-phase commit locks.

spark.summary: A saga breaks a global transaction into local transactions with compensations; orchestration centralizes flow while choreography uses events.
spark.keyTakeaway: Model forward steps and compensations explicitly—partial failure is normal, not exceptional.

concept.whyItMatters: Microservices cannot hold cross-service locks; sagas are how checkout, travel booking, and billing stay coherent.
whenNotToUse: Compensations are impossible for the domain
keyPoints: Compensations are business operations, not rollbacks

examples.title: Travel reservation
examples.scenario: Reserve flight, hotel, and car across vendors.
examples.outcome: Failed hotel booking triggers flight cancellation compensation.

failureModes.name: Missing compensation
failureModes.description: Forward step succeeds but rollback path undefined.
failureModes.mitigation: Design compensations before shipping forward actions.

commonMistakes: Treating sagas as “distributed transactions” with locks

deepDive.markdownContent:
## Sagas

Prefer compensating transactions over blocking 2PC across services.

caseStudy.problem: Checkout spanning inventory, payment, and shipping

relationships.description: Sagas trade strong global isolation for availability.
Every saga step must tolerate retries.
